Currently, it can only be spawned in [[Sandbox Mode|Sandbox]] mode if the player has the Sandbox Plus+ [[Gamepasses|gamepass]]. While it has low health for its debut, it is quite fast. While the '''Lead Balloon''' is in the air, it cannot collide with [[units]], or be detected by most ground towers and units. It is also a [[Lead (Attribute)|Lead]] enemy, meaning it cannot be damaged by towers without lead detection. This severely reduces the amount of towers that can harm the '''Lead Balloon'''. With its balloons popped, it is no longer a [[Flying]] enemy. However, despite having no visible metal coverings, it is still a [[Lead (Attribute)|Lead]] enemy. The '''Lead Balloon''' can be spawned from the [[Mystery]] upon its death in [[Hardcore Mode|Hardcore]] mode, wave 40 onwards. ==Appearance== The '''Lead Balloon''' is a faceless humanoid with reflective dark green skin, and a reflective dark grey torso and legs. It has three lead balloons tied to its back, which, after taking enough damage, pop into yellow particles and drops it lower to the ground. When it loses all shield health, all the balloons would have popped and the '''Lead Balloon''' would become grounded, removing its flying attribute and making it walk along the path. ==Strategy== This strategy refers to the state of the game while the '''Lead Balloon''' still appeared in the [[Hardcore Mode|Hardcore]] mode. *While the '''Lead Balloon''' is floating, the '''Lead Balloon''' is a lead and flying enemy. However, [[Toxic Gunner]] is an event tower that is currently unobtainable outside of special offers. *The [[Ace Pilot]], [[Mortar]] and [[Pursuit]] can detect and damage the '''Lead Balloon''' with its splash damage. **However, the [[Ace Pilot]]'s projectiles explode on the ground, limiting the damage dealt to the '''Lead Balloon'''. Fast and tanky with Giant bosses in the back.|[[Commander (Narrator)|Commander]] dialogue on Wave 28 ([[Pizza Party|Pizzeria]] before the mini rework)}} }} __TOC__ ==Description== The '''Balloon Kid''' is an enemy only found in [[Pizza Party]]. It has a mediocre amount of health and an above average speed. However, it holds a balloon which it uses to float in the air, making it a [[Flying]] enemy. This also means that it cannot collide with units, as well as being undetectable by the majority of towers and units. ==Appearance== The '''Balloon Kid''' is a robot that resembles a child. It has tan skin, grey pants, black shoes, a striped red and blue torso, sleeves, propeller hat and a balloon that it holds, which it uses to float in the air. It has a red nose and the left side of its face is torn open. It also has two red buttons on its torso. Its propeller hat's propeller spins as the '''Balloon Kid''' flies. It makes a popping sound on death. ==Mutation== {| class="tds-table align-center mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" style="width: 300px; margin: 0 auto;" ! colspan="2" |Mutation |- !Percentage !Increase |- |6% |30 |- !Wave !Health |- |29 |1,280 |- |30 |1,310 |- |31 |1,340 |- |32 |1,370 |- |33 |1,400 |- |34 |1,430 |- |35 |1,460 |- |36 |1,490 |- |37 |1,520 |- |38 |1,550 |- |39 |1,580 |- |40 |1,610 |} ==Strategy== *Towers with flying detection are the best way to deal with the '''Balloon Kid'''. **The [[Ranger]] and [[Golden Soldier]] are very strong options. ***The [[Militant]] is another option, but may be unreliable due to its lower DPS. **As these spawn in hordes, the [[Executioner]] and [[Mortar]] can be quite effective at clearing them out. **The [[Ace Pilot]] and [[Pursuit]] can deal with '''Balloon Kids''' fairly effectively, but be mindful of their circling and targeting mechanics, which could let some '''Balloon Kids''' past. **Alternatively, if you do not have any towers with flying detection, you can use a [[UAV]] to make other towers target '''Balloon Kids'''. ***Do note that the [[UAV]] only lasts 30 seconds and can only be used four times, so you cannot completely rely on it for flying detection, though it can allow you to survive a few waves without it. **You can also use the [[Commander]]'s ''Support Caravan'' ability to spawn in [[Gunner APC]]s and [[Missile APC]]s if your main DPS does not have flying detection. *There are many towers that do not have flying detection but can damage '''Balloon Kids''' in other ways. Most of these methods are not viable ways to deal with the '''Balloon Kids'''. Another detectable enemy must be nearby for these to happen. **Explosions from towers can damage the '''Balloon Kid''' indirectly. ***Only the [[Mortar]], [[Ace Pilot]] and [[Pursuit]] can directly target '''Balloon Kids''' with splash damage. Others require a nearby detectable enemy. **Some ground towers, like the [[Gladiator]], can hit the '''Balloon Kid''' while it is in the air, if they are on a high platform or leverage, though this is extremely unlikely to occur. **The [[Brawler]] tower is able to hit the '''Balloon Kid''' using its ''Reposition'' ability. ==Gallery== {{Gallery| {{GalleryHeader|Corpse Variants}} CorpseBalloonKid.png|Second [[Corpse (Enemy)|Corpse]] variant, current version (12 March 2025 – Present) {{GalleryHeader|Promotional Images}} HalloweenPI4.jpg|'''Balloon Kid''' on a promotional image. {{GalleryHeader|Trailers}} Tower Defense

Some inherited from spawner enemy }} ==Description== The '''Corpse''' is an enemy that only appears when spawned through the [[Corpse (Attribute)|Corpse]] attribute. Uniquely, its statistics are actually heavily based on the enemy that summoned it, instead of having its own statistics, though it does have some statistics that do not change. This is because the '''Corpse''' is not its own enemy, it is actually the enemy it spawned from with a changed display name and altered statistics. Most notably, it has 100% defense, and it has the [[Corpse (Attribute)|Corpse]], [[Stun Immunity]] and [[Burn Immunity]] attributes. Its health is 75% of the enemy that it spawned from. Additionally, some of the attributes the enemy it spawned from are also inherited. The only exception to this is [[Hidden (Attribute)|Hidden]], which is removed upon the enemy's death. ==Appearance== The '''Corpse''' does not have a consistent appearance, as the model it uses is based on the enemy it spawned from, though it does have certain characteristics which are consistent between them all. The '''Corpse''' is the body of the enemy it spawned from made entirely out of black molten rocks. Any images present on the enemy, such as faces, will remain on them even as a '''Corpse'''. ==Strategy== *The '''Corpse''' is not a threatening enemy, as it cannot move to the entrance, meaning losing to it is impossible. Its main purpose is to act as a shield for enemies behind it. **However, it can be relatively annoying with its 100% defense and tendency to distract towers from attacking actual enemies. **Towers like the [[Electroshocker]] or [[Toxic Gunner]] can be used to drop its defense, as it is very high. The [[Pyromancer]] cannot be used since it has [[Burn Immunity]]. **Towers like the [[Ranger]] or [[Mortar]] can be used to take care of any corpses that are too far away from your main defenses with their high range. *The '''Corpse''' is required to be killed before a match can end. **Waves can be skipped while only '''Corpses''' are on the path, as that still grants the wave clear bonus. Additionally, infinite waves cannot be skipped at all. ***If you have the [[DJ Booth]], you can exploit this by repeatedly using its ''Drop The Beat'' ability on Green track to make as much cash as you want. *As the '''Corpse''' is technically not a unique, summoned enemy, but instead the slightly altered version of the enemy it spawned from, the [[Cowboy]] is able to generate cash from it. ==Gallery== {{Gallery| {{GalleryHeader|Previous Variants}} MoltenCorpseMolten.png|First version (11 December 2024 – 12 March 2025) {{GalleryHeader|Promot

[[Frost Invasion Event|Frost Invasion]] |first_wave_appearance = 12 (Originally) |base_hp = [[File:HealthIcon.png|20px|Health]]5,000 |speed = [[File:SpeedIcon.png|20px|Speed]]Slightly Slow (2) |defense = {{Defense}}50% |hidden = No |fly = No |ghost = No |lead = No |immunity = {{Attr|Freeze}} }} __TOC__ ==Description== The '''Deep Freeze''' was an enemy that appeared exclusively in [[Outpost 32 (Frost Invasion)|Outpost 32]] as part of the [[Frost Invasion Event]]. It can now only appear in [[Sandbox Mode|Sandbox]] mode. It had a high amount of health, but walked slowly. It also had 50% [[defense]] which reduced most forms of damage. The '''Deep Freeze''' could not be frozen as it had [[Freeze Immunity]]. ==Appearance== The '''Deep Freeze''' has baby blue skin, and white snow textured torso and legs. A tumor can be seen on its head. White spikes can be seen coming out of its shoulders. White ice chunks can be seen sticking out of its arms and legs. Its head is slightly tilted downwards and had a twisted left leg. ==Event Strategy== As this enemy only appears through [[Sandbox Mode|Sandbox]] mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without [[Sandbox Mode|Sandbox]] mode in [[Outpost 32 (Frost Invasion)|Outpost 32]] is listed instead. *You should use high DPS towers, like the [[Accelerator]], [[Ranger]], [[Minigunner]] or [[Turret]], to defeat the '''Deep Freeze'''. **However, be aware that due to the 50% [[defense]], it will take longer than normal to defeat the '''Deep Freeze'''. **You may want to use the [[Commander]]'s ''Call to Arms'' ability to boost the firerate of these towers. *[[Defense]] is ignored by splash damage, meaning that towers and [[units]] that deal splash damage will do 100% damage if the '''Deep Freeze''' is caught in the epicenter. **This makes towers like the [[Rocketeer]] and [[Mortar]] very useful against the '''Deep Freeze'''. **Upon collision, [[units]], like the [[Railgun Tank]], will ignore [[defense]] and deal full collision damage towards the '''Deep Freeze'''. *As the '''Deep Freeze''' has quite high defense, you can use a Level 2 [[Pyromancer]] to lower its defense, allowing your towers to deal more damage to it. **Additionally, as with all enemies in the [[Frost Invasion Event]], the [[Pyromancer]] deals double fire damage to the '''Deep Freeze''' (though normal damage is not doubled). **You can also use other defense dropping towers, like the [[Electroshocker]] or [[Freezer]]. However, these are more expensive and less effective as they only drop 20% defense. *The '''Deep Freeze''' cannot be frozen by the [[Freezer]], [[Frost Blaster]] or [[Sledger]]. **If you want to slow the '''Deep Freeze''' down, then you must use the [[Electroshocker]] or [[Toxic Gunner]]. ==Gallery== {{Gallery| {{GalleryHeader|Corpse Variants}} CorpseLegacyDeepFreeze.png|Second [[Corpse (Enemy)|Corpse]] variant, current version (12 March 2025 – Present) {{GalleryHeader|Trailers}} Tower Defense Simulator Frost Invasion Trailer|'''Deep Freeze''' in the game trailer. {{GalleryHeader|Miscellaneous}} FrostInvasionDeepFreezeIconIG.png|'''Deep Freeze''' on its [[Index]] icon. }} ==Trivia== *This version of the '''Deep Freeze''' was quite similar to the [[Deep Freeze (Village of Despair)|Deep Freeze]] from [[Village of Despair]] in appearance. **Another version of the [[Deep Freeze (Pre-MEGA)|Deep Freeze]

==Description==
The '''Deep Freeze''' was an ice elemental [[Enemies|enemy]]. Compared to the [[Frozen (Pre-MEGA)|Frozen]], the '''Deep Freeze''' was slightly slower, but it had more health. The '''Deep Freeze''' was immune to the [[Freezer]]'s basic freeze, but not its ''Ice Drop''.

==Appearance==
{{Tabber
|Version 2
|The second version of the '''Deep Freeze''' had sky blue skin and was faceless. Its torso and legs were marble blue. It also had rusty blue armbands. A tumor could be seen on the '''Deep Freeze's''' head.
|Version 1
|This version of the '''Deep Freeze''' had blue skin and was faceless. Its torso and legs were black ice. It also had rusty blue armbands. A tumor could be seen on the '''Deep Freeze's''' head.
}}

==Strategy==
*[[Rocketeer|Rocketers]] and [[Demoman|Demomen]] can easily wipe out hordes of '''Deep Freezes'''.
**The [[Ranger|Outlaw]], with the [[Commander]]'s [[Firerate Buff]], can also be helpful in defeating this.
*The [[Pyromancer]] can be used to slow the '''Deep Freeze''' down to allow your towers more time to kill it.
*Despite being an ice elemental enemy, this can be frozen by the [[Freezer]]'s ''Ice Drop'' ability.
**However, the [[Freezer]] cannot freeze the '''Deep Freeze''' with its normal attack.

==Description==
The '''Deep Freeze''' was an ice elemental enemy. It appeared in [[Village of Despair]] as part of the [[Christmas 2019 Event]].

For its debut, the '''Deep Freeze''' had a high amount of health, higher than the [[Frozen (Village of Despair)|Frozen]]. However, it walked quite slowly. The '''Deep Freeze''' could not be frozen by the [[Freezer]] and [[Frost Blaster]] as it had [[Freeze Immunity]].

The '''Deep Freeze''' could also have been spawned by [[Krampus (Village of Despair)|Krampus]].

==Appearance==
The '''Deep Freeze''' was larger than the [[Frozen (Village of Despair)|Frozen]]. It had blue skin, and its torso and legs were white marble. The '''Deep Freeze'''  also had a spiky neckguard, while its back was also spiky. White ice chunks could be seen sticking out of the '''Deep Freeze's''' arms and legs. On the side of its head, a tumor could be seen.

==Strategy==
*The '''Deep Freeze''' is the first high health enemy you encounter in [[Village of Despair]]. Make sure you have enough [[Minigunner]]s and [[Ranger|Outlaws]] to deal with this.
**A [[Commander]] may also be required when you first encounter this.
*The '''Deep Freeze''' is slower than the [[Snowman (Village of Despair)|Snowman]] and [[Burnt Gingerbread]], meaning that those enemies can pass the '''Deep Freeze''' and act as a shield.
**In this case, it is best to have a [[Rocketeer]] on hand to defeat the weaker enemies.
*The '''Deep Freeze''' is completely immune to the [[Freezer]] and [[Frost Blaster]], including the [[Freezer]]'s ''Ice Age''.
**If you want to slow it down, then you can use the [[Pyromancer]].

==Description==
'''Defense''' is a status value given to certain enemies and units. Enemies may spawn with this naturally, or be granted this through a litany of means.

==Mechanics==
There are two types of defense statistic. The main defense statistic is ''Percentage Defense'' which is used to calculate ''Effective Damage''.

''Percentage Defense'' is the actual defense percentage you see on an enemy or unit. However, this does not mean that if an enemy has 50% defense damage dealt towards it will be decreased 50%. In reality, the number listed is far closer to the percentage of additional health that '''Defense''' gives it.

''Effective Damage'' is the actual damage dealt towards an enemy by a tower once ''Percentage Defense'' is applied. ''Effective Damage'' is calculated by calculating

::<big>'''Original Damage ÷ (1 + Percentage Defense)'''</big>

where ''Percentage Defense'' is changed from a percentage into its equivalent decimal number (for instance, 50% would be 0.5 in decimal form). For example, a tower that deals 100 damage attacking an enemy with 50% defense would deal 67 damage as 100 ÷ (1 + 0.5) = 66.67 to two decimal places. Due to ''Effective Damage'' always being rounded up to the nearest integer, 66.67 rounds up to 67. Prior to the [[v1.1.0|Entity System Update]], ''Effective Damage'' was always rounded down to the nearest integer.

Unit defense works identically to enemy defense, reducing damage from enemy abilities and collision.

A list of certain ''Percentage Defense'' values and how much damage they actually reduce has been provided below. This is not a comprehensive list and the values may not be fully accurate due to how the game rounds up the damage, making the values occasionally lower.

===Countering Defense===
'''Defense''' can reduce the damage output of most towers significantly.

There are a couple of towers and consumables that can melt the ''Percentage Defense'' value of enemies, allowing your towers to deal more damage. A few certain towers can also ignore defense. There are two types of defense melting towers. The first has them decrease ''Total Defense'' by a certain percentage. However, if the [[Pyromancer]], which melts defense by 50%, is decreasing defense of [[Fallen Hero]], which has 50% defense, this does not mean its defense will be lowered to 0%. Instead, it is decreased by 25% defense, as which is 50% of 50% defense. The defense removal can stack, so the [[Pyromancer]] and [[Electroshocker]] can together remove 70% ''Percentage Defense'', but two [[Pyromancer]]s cannot remove 100% ''Percentage Defense''. Instead, only 50% ''Percentage Defense'' can be melted. Additionally, defense melting from burn cannot stack with other burn towers, freeze defense melting cannot stack with other freeze towers and poison defense melting cannot stack with other poison towers.

The second type has them decrease ''Total Defense'' by a flat amount. For example, the [[DJ Booth]] at maximum power can melt 25% defense. This means that when melting defense of the [[Fallen Giant]], it will will melt its defense from 60% to 35%.

Both forms of defense melting do not interfere with each other and can stack. For example, if the [[DJ Booth]] decreases the [[Vindicator (Legacy)|Vindicator]]'s defense from 100% to 75%, the [[Pyromancer]] will reduce it from 75% to 25%, which is the same decrease (50% less defense) as if [[DJ Booth]] did not affect it. Likewise, if the [[Pyromancer]] decreases the [[Vindicator (Legacy)|Vindicator]]'s defense from 100% to 50%, the [[DJ Booth]] will still be able to decrease it by 25%, from 50% to 25%.
